title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government responds to the Committee’s 2020 report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards by outlining a strategy to create clear, enforceable standards that promote AI safety, transparency, and accountability. It commits to strengthening regulations, fostering stakeholder collaboration, and ensuring that AI systems meet rigorous quality and ethical benchmarks.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is setting rules to govern how artificial intelligence can be used in creating, marking, and administering qualifications, ensuring that AI tools do not compromise the fairness or reliability of assessment. The policy seeks to maintain public confidence in qualifications by requiring clear evidence of AI impact, safeguards against bias, and transparency in how AI is employed.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how AI systems are trained on copyrighted works, assessing the legal and ethical risks involved. It provides policy recommendations to balance fostering AI innovation with protecting creators’ rights.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a formal reply to the House of Lords Select Committee’s AI report, outlining its views on the report’s findings. It signals a commitment to strengthen AI safety, ethics, and innovation while addressing the risks highlighted in the committee’s recommendations.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the roles, responsibilities, and scope of a committee tasked with reviewing artificial intelligence in relation to public standards. It also includes frequently asked questions to clarify the committee’s objectives, procedures, and expected outcomes.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of Artificial Intelligence, outlining its views and recommendations on how AI should be regulated. The submission focuses on key issues such as accountability, transparency, and the development of appropriate regulatory frameworks.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy explores how artificial intelligence is changing the rules and safety standards for medical products, highlighting the need for clear, up-to-date guidance. It outlines how to apply the AI White Paper principles to streamline regulation, promote innovation, and protect patients in the healthcare industry.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the organization the world's most effective, efficient, trusted and influential AI‑driven defence body for its size. It outlines a vision for developing advanced AI capabilities, ensuring ethical use, and integrating AI across defence operations to maintain a competitive edge.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will collaborate with the transport sector to unlock the benefits of AI while carefully managing risks. It focuses on encouraging innovation, boosting efficiency, and ensuring AI technologies are deployed safely and responsibly across transportation services.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report examines how copyright‑protected works are being used to train AI systems, assessing whether these uses comply with the Data (Use and Access) Act’s requirements. It highlights current practices, identifies legal and ethical challenges, and offers recommendations to improve transparency, fairness, and respect for creators’ rights.
